events.title: Justinian promulgates the first Code of Roman law
events.description: Emperor Justinian issued the Codex Justinianus, gathering imperial constitutions into a single authoritative collection. Revised in 534, it became the core of the Corpus Juris Civilis that shaped European law.
events.html: Emperor Justinian issued the Codex Justinianus, gathering imperial constitutions into a single authoritative collection. Revised in 534, it became the core of the Corpus Juris Civilis that shaped European law.

events.title: Charles IV founds the university in Prague
events.description: Charles IV, King of Bohemia, issued the charter founding a university in Prague, the first in Central Europe. Now Charles University, it later became a centre of the Hussite reform movement.
events.html: Charles IV, King of Bohemia, issued the charter founding a university in Prague, the first in Central Europe. Now Charles University, it later became a centre of the Hussite reform movement.

events.title: Highwayman Dick Turpin is hanged at York
events.description: Dick Turpin, convicted of horse theft, was hanged on the Knavesmire at York. The violent robber was later romanticised in fiction as a dashing gentleman of the road.
events.html: Dick Turpin, convicted of horse theft, was hanged on the Knavesmire at York. The violent robber was later romanticised in fiction as a dashing gentleman of the road.

events.title: Congress creates the Mississippi Territory
events.description: The US Congress organised the Mississippi Territory on land ceded by Spain in 1795. It was later enlarged and divided into the states of Mississippi and Alabama.
events.html: The US Congress organised the Mississippi Territory on land ceded by Spain in 1795. It was later enlarged and divided into the states of Mississippi and Alabama.

events.title: John Walker records the first sale of friction matches
events.description: Stockton-on-Tees chemist John Walker sold his newly invented 'friction lights', matches struck against sandpaper. He never patented them, and others soon copied the idea.
events.html: Stockton-on-Tees chemist John Walker sold his newly invented 'friction lights', matches struck against sandpaper. He never patented them, and others soon copied the idea.

events.title: Italy invades Albania
events.description: Mussolini's forces landed at Durrës and other ports, and within days King Zog had fled. Albania was joined to the Italian crown, and the invasion later served as a base for Italy's attack on Greece.

events.title: Genocide against the Tutsi begins in Rwanda
events.description: Hours after President Habyarimana's aircraft was shot down, extremists began killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu. In about 100 days an estimated 500,000 to 800,000 people were murdered.
